page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n4 family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel core with hyper-threading (2 threads per core) on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It has dedicated CPU allocation and includes an L3 cache size of 260 MB, alongside 48 KB L1d and 2 MB L2 caches. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core performance paired with weaker multi-core and memory throughput. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance score is 1684.29, and the Geekbench single-core score is 1834.0, both falling into the average category. However, multi-core performance is limited, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2251.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 1714.68. Memory bandwidth is relatively low, measuring 19.35 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 12.78 GB/sec for large-block write operations.

Given the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and its performance profile, the n4-standard-2 is suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads. It supports advanced vector and matrix extensions, such as AVX-512 and AMX, which assist in basic integer, cryptography, and low-intensity vector operations. However, its weak multi-core scaling, lower memory bandwidth, and poor database operations score of 1259.2 on PassMark make it less optimal for high-throughput database hosting, heavy compilation, or intensive multi-threaded applications. It is best utilized for basic web serving, text processing, and lightweight background tasks.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical Intel core and 8.0 GB of RAM. It includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX, though it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show average single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1834.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1684.29. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 2251.0 and a large-block read memory bandwidth of 19.35 GB/sec. This resource profile makes the instance cost-efficient for entry-level general-purpose tasks, basic text processing, and low-throughput web serving, while rendering it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or heavy multi-threaded computing.
